selected.title: Inflation surges more than expected ahead of RBA meeting
selected.summary: Australia's inflation rate picked up more than expected in September, increasing expectations of an interest rate hike next week.
selected.why: Surprising CPI data beat shifting RBA monetary policy and interest rate expectations.

( AAP: Alan Porritt ) In short: Inflation rose to 4.3 per cent in the year to September, driven by housing and transport costs. Underlying inflation also edged up, after August's figures were revised lower. What's next? Markets now overwhelmingly expect the Reserve Bank to hike interest rates next Tuesday. abc.net.au/news/inflation-september-cpi-ahead-of-november-interest-rate-call/107317382 Link copied Share Share article Australia's inflation rate rose more than expected in September, raising expectations of an interest rate hike next week. The consumer price index rose to 0.8 per cent in the month, from 0.4 per cent in August, taking annual inflation to 4.3 per cent, up from 4 per cent a month earlier, the Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) said. "Housing was the largest contributor to annual inflation in September, rising by 5.2 per cent," ABS head of price statistics Rachael McCririck said. Transport also drove annual inflation higher, largely due to higher fuel prices, which rose 9.4 per cent in September. The annual trimmed mean, a measure of underlying inflation, also picked up to 3.6 per cent in September. The August trimmed mean was revised lower to 3.5 per cent. The increase in underlying inflation was despite fuel prices being excluded from the trimmed mean due to their volatility. Following the CPI release, market pricing for a November interest rate hike surged, putting the chance of a 0.25 per cent increase next week at about 85 per cent, according to Bloomberg data. KPMG Australia chief economist Brendan Rynne described the inflation figures as "the last data point necessary for the RBA to increase the cash rate for a fifth time this year".
